title: 了: change (now it's…)
summary: Lets you say a situation has changed by adding 了 at the end, as in 天冷了.
explanation:
了 at the end of a sentence can show a NEW situation: 天冷了 'It's got cold (now).' 我不忙了 'I'm not busy any more' and 他十岁了 'He's ten now' work the same way.

With 不 it means 'not any more': 我不喝茶了 'I don't drink tea any more.' 现在八点了 'It's eight o'clock now.' This 了 is about change, not about a finished action.

examples.zh: 现在八点了，我们上课吧。
examples.en: It's eight now, let's start class.

mistakes.why: This 了 goes at the end of the sentence.
'Not any more' is 不 … 了, not 没 … 了.

why: Correct: 了 at the end shows a new situation.
吗 would make it a question.
没 … 了 is wrong for 'not any more'.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'My daughter is five now'?
why: This adds 是 and 吗 and isn't a statement.

exercises.why: 了 at the very end shows the change: now it is snowing.

exercises.en: It's ten o'clock now; time to sleep.
why: Correct: 了 shows the time has come.
吧 already ends the second part.
呢 doesn't show a change here.

exercises.prompt: Your friend was ill but is fine now. You say:
why: Without 了 there's no sense of change.
没 … 了 doesn't work here.
